quote: until I saw that it was embarrassingly obvious
content: The essay's criterion for real understanding is the moment the wave equation became "embarrassingly obvious." That feeling is exactly the signal the rest of the sequence says not to trust. The sense of understanding is a poor guide to whether an explanation is correct or even coherent (Trout 2002), and people are systematically overconfident that they understand mechanisms until asked to produce them (Rozenblit & Keil 2002). Nothing in the essay tests whether the older Yudkowsky's understanding of "wave" was better than the nine-year-old's beyond that it felt so. An essay against mistaking verbal behavior for knowledge offers, as its example of knowledge, a reported feeling.

quote: putting in numbers and getting out results that control your anticipation of particular experiences
content: Physics-education research found this criterion to be the wrong one. Students who can solve quantitative problems, putting in numbers and getting out results, routinely fail the same physics stated qualitatively, and solving a thousand traditional problems does not fix the qualitative misconceptions (Kim & Pak 2002; Hestenes, Wells & Swackhamer 1992). The failure mode the field actually identified is computation without conceptual understanding, which is the exact profile the essay calls understanding. Conversely, most of what a working physicist understands about turbulence or the weather is not something they can compute. "Use the diffusion equation" is a password too; it just has more symbols in it.

quote: which must be the correct answer because the teacher heard a physicist emit the same sound-vibrations
content: By the standard of the sequence's own What Is Evidence?, the physicist's honest assurance that light is waves is evidence, rational beliefs are "contagious among honest folk," and the student who believes it on testimony holds a rationally justified belief. The mockery here of belief transmitted by hearing a physicist "emit sound-vibrations" contradicts that essay directly. The student in fact learned something checkable: a physicist, whose community has tested the claim, asserts it, which is how nearly all scientific knowledge is held by nearly everyone (Hardwig 1991). The essay's real complaint is that the student cannot derive the wave equation, which is true of almost everyone who correctly believes light is waves.
